primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Abetalipoproteinemia due to biallelic MTTP pathogenic variants
mechanism: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is required in enterocytes and hepatocytes for assembly and secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins. MTTP deficiency prevents formation/secretion of chylomicrons and VLDL, producing severe hypolipidemia, fat malabsorption, and fat-soluble-vitamin deficiency.
vignette: A 7-year-old girl has chronic steatorrhea, poor growth, progressive gait instability, and diminished deep-tendon reflexes. Peripheral smear shows acanthocytes. Plasma apoB and LDL cholesterol are nearly absent. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in MTTP.
lead: Which of the following normal cellular processes is most directly impaired in this patient?
correct: Assembly and secretion of apoB-containing chylomicrons and very-low-density lipoproteins
distractors: Cholesterol efflux from peripheral cells to nascent apoA-I particles
Esterification of free cholesterol within high-density lipoprotein particles
Receptor-mediated endocytosis of circulating low-density lipoprotein
Hydrolysis of triglycerides in circulating chylomicrons by capillary lipoprotein lipase
distractor_notes: ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux to apoA-I is defective in Tangier disease, not MTTP-related abetalipoproteinemia.
LCAT esterifies cholesterol on HDL; LCAT deficiency does not prevent apoB-lipoprotein assembly in enterocytes and hepatocytes.
LDL receptor defects impair LDL clearance and cause hypercholesterolemia rather than near-absence of apoB-containing particles.
Lipoprotein lipase acts on circulating triglyceride-rich lipoproteins after they have been secreted; the primary defect here is failure to assemble and secrete those particles.
key_expl: MTTP transfers lipid during formation of apoB-containing lipoproteins in the endoplasmic reticulum. Without functional MTTP, enterocytes cannot secrete normal chylomicrons and hepatocytes cannot secrete normal VLDL. The resulting deficiency of apoB-containing lipoproteins causes fat malabsorption and fat-soluble-vitamin deficiency, which can produce neurologic and retinal manifestations.
objective: Explain abetalipoproteinemia as MTTP deficiency causing failure of apoB-containing chylomicron and VLDL assembly/secretion.
